blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Succession planning, when taken seriously, is among the most consequential decisions any board ever makes. A single CEO succession can determine the direction of a company for the next decade, and in the case of family businesses, for generations. Yet very few organisations treat it with the discipline it deserves.

The classic failure is to confuse succession planning with naming a replacement. A genuine succession process is a multi-year programme of developmental exposure, stress-tested through real decisions and observed across multiple business cycles. It is designed to reveal character, not merely to validate reputation.

There is also a less discussed dimension: the quiet politics of succession. Strong incumbents sometimes, consciously or not, obstruct the emergence of credible successors. Boards that fail to confront that dynamic early may find themselves with only one realistic candidate when the moment comes — which is not a succession plan, but the absence of one.

items.q: According to the text, why is CEO succession so consequential?
options: It can shape a company's direction for a decade or, in family firms, for generations
It is the most expensive process a board undertakes
It is legally required of every listed company
It always triggers a change of ownership
items.why: "can determine the direction of a company for the next decade, and in the case of family businesses, for generations."

items.q: What is described as "the classic failure" in succession planning?
options: Promoting too many candidates at once
Announcing the successor too publicly
Confusing succession planning with simply naming a replacement
Spending too much money on external consultants
items.why: "The classic failure is to confuse succession planning with naming a replacement."

items.q: The text says a genuine succession process is designed to reveal character rather than validate reputation. This most strongly suggests that…
options: boards should ignore a candidate's track record entirely
reputation is a reliable proxy for character
a strong public reputation is not proof that a candidate is ready
character can be assessed from a single interview
items.why: Inferência: se é preciso revelar caráter em vez de validar reputação, a reputação sozinha não garante prontidão.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A single well-regarded candidate on the shortlist means the board has a solid plan
Succession should be observed across several business cycles
Character matters more than reputation in choosing a leader
Incumbents can quietly hinder the rise of successors
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que um único candidato realista "is not a succession plan, but the absence of one".

items.q: What does the phrase "consciously or not" imply about strong incumbents obstructing successors?
options: The obstruction is always a deliberate political strategy
Incumbents rarely have any influence over succession
The behaviour may happen even without the incumbent intending it
Only weak incumbents block their successors
items.why: Inferência: "consciously or not" indica que o bloqueio pode ocorrer sem intenção deliberada.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o plano de sucessão ao comitê de nomeação. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm putting in front of you today is a five-year plan, not a shortlist. I want to be clear about that distinction from the outset, because it shapes everything that follows.

Our current CEO has led this business for twelve years, and by any measure has served us well. But twelve years is a long tenure, and it may prove harder than we expect to develop credible successors in his shadow. That is not a criticism of him — it is simply the reality of a strong incumbent. Talented people either wait, or they leave.

So my proposal is deliberate exposure. Over the next three years, we rotate two or three internal candidates through genuinely difficult mandates — a turnaround, a major acquisition, a downturn. We watch how they behave when the decision is hard and the outcome is uncertain. That, far more than any interview, is likely to tell us who is ready.

And I'd ask the committee to hold its nerve. The temptation, when the moment finally arrives, is to reach for the safest name. But if we've done this properly, we won't need to guess.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What distinction does Sophie insist on "from the outset"?
options: That external candidates are excluded
That the board, not the CEO, decides
That the plan is confidential
That this is a five-year plan, not a shortlist
items.why: "What I'm putting in front of you today is a five-year plan, not a shortlist."

items.q: Why does Sophie say it may prove harder than expected to develop successors?
options: Because the company lacks talented people
Because the board refuses to invest in training
Because the market is in a downturn
Because a strong, long-serving incumbent casts a shadow over emerging candidates
items.why: "it may prove harder than we expect to develop credible successors in his shadow… the reality of a strong incumbent."

items.q: What does Sophie propose as the core of the plan?
options: Running a series of formal interviews
Asking the current CEO to name his successor
Hiring an external CEO immediately
Rotating candidates through genuinely difficult mandates over three years
items.why: "we rotate two or three internal candidates through genuinely difficult mandates — a turnaround, a major acquisition, a downturn."

items.q: When Sophie says "Talented people either wait, or they leave," she is implying that…
options: a dominant incumbent can quietly cost the firm its best future leaders
the company should not hire ambitious people
patience is the main quality of a good successor
loyalty is more important than talent
items.why: Inferência: sob um titular forte, os talentosos ou esperam ou vão embora — o incumbente pode custar futuros líderes.

items.q: What does Sophie mean when she asks the committee to "hold its nerve"?
options: To keep the plan secret from the CEO
To avoid any disagreement in the meeting
To resist the urge to pick the safest name when the moment arrives
To move faster than the five-year timeline
items.why: Inferência: ela alerta contra "reach for the safest name" — pede que confiem no processo em vez de ceder ao medo.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The board finally began serious succession planning after a near-miss." Succession planning is…
options: preparing, over time, for the orderly handover of leadership
the annual review of executive salaries
the sale of the company to a competitor
the process of firing an underperforming CEO
items.why: Succession planning = planejamento de sucessão: preparar a transição de liderança com antecedência.

items.q: "After twelve years, the incumbent was reluctant to discuss his own departure." The incumbent is…
options: the person currently holding the role
an external consultant
the newest board member
the leading candidate to take over
items.why: Incumbent = titular atual, quem ocupa o cargo no momento.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We rotated her through a turnaround and an acquisition to see how she performs when ___."
options: outsourced
shortlisted
reimbursed
stress-tested
items.why: Stress-tested = testado sob pressão, em decisões reais e difíceis.

items.q: Board dynamics is best described as…
options: the way power, relationships and influence actually play out among directors
the legal duties written into the company's bylaws
the total compensation paid to directors
the schedule of quarterly board meetings
items.why: Board dynamics = dinâmica do conselho: como poder e relações realmente operam entre os conselheiros.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "With only one realistic name on the list, we do not have a plan — we have the ___ of one."
options: mandate
legacy
absence
continuity
items.why: Ecoa a lição: um único candidato realista "is not a succession plan, but the absence of one".

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de conselho e comitês de sucessão. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The committee still has to sign off on the succession timeline." To sign off on means to…
options: leak to the press
quietly ignore
reopen for debate
formally approve
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "A dominant incumbent can stand in the way of a credible successor." This means the incumbent can…
options: resign in favour of the successor
actively support the successor
obstruct or block the successor's rise
mentor the successor privately
items.why: Stand in the way of = atrapalhar, obstruir a ascensão de alguém.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on naming a successor so early." They…
options: forgot to read the proposal
endorsed the idea at once
resisted or challenged the idea
delegated the decision to the CEO
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The board approved the plan but never followed through on the rotations." They…
options: expanded the plan considerably
failed to see the plan through to the end
carried the plan to completion
cancelled it publicly
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não fizeram isso.

items.q: "When the CEO retires, the board wants a smooth handover." A handover is…
options: an orderly transfer of responsibility from one leader to the next
a public shareholder vote
a hostile takeover by a rival firm
a temporary suspension of the role
items.why: Handover = passagem de bastão, transferência ordenada de responsabilidade.
